title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Five Revenue Engines, One Vertically Integrated Backbone

epigraph.quote: Understanding a pharmaceutical conglomerate requires tracing a single molecule from the fermentation vat all the way to the hospital pharmacy shelf.
epigraph.author: Pharmaceutical Sector Underwriting Principle

web_blocks.html: Aurobindo Pharma earned ₹33,653 crore in FY26 revenue across five reporting segments [1][2]. USA Formulations led at 42.8%, followed by Europe Formulations at 30.7% [2][6]. APIs contributed 12.0%, Growth Markets 10.4%, and Anti-Retrovirals (ARV) 4.1% [2][6]. Growth picked up sharply in H1 FY27 (April–September 2026). Q1 FY27 sales rose 16% YoY to ₹9,150 crore, while Q2 FY27 hit a record ₹10,263 crore (+23.9% YoY) as US and European launches scaled together [1][3].

web_blocks.takeaway: Europe (+23.4%) and ARV (+31.9%) offset the FY26 gRevlimid cliff in the US (-2.7%), while Q2 FY27 marked a broad-based US + Europe inflection (+24% consolidated YoY) [1][2][3][6].

web_blocks.html: 1. USA Formulations (₹14,408 Cr | 42.8% of FY26 sales): This unit covers oral solids (tablets, capsules, inhalers, controlled drugs) plus sterile injectables and oncology drugs [2][12]. Products reach market via subsidiary Eugia Pharma Specialities and US arms Aurobindo Pharma USA and AuroMedics [2][12]. In FY26, US sales fell 2.7% YoY as high-margin gRevlimid (lenalidomide) volumes tapered, including a ~₹550 crore drop in Q1 FY26 [2][22]. Even so, the core portfolio bounced back fast. In Q2 FY27, US revenue jumped 25% YoY to ₹4,555 crore ($477 million) on 10 new launches, led by gAdvair and ADQUEY, Aurobindo's first US New Chemical Entity (NCE) [3]. Eugia is tracking above $500 million in FY27 sales, though USFDA remediation at Unit III caps new US injectable approvals [4][8].

Concrete End-to-End Example (USA): Consider how generic amoxicillin-clavulanate or metformin reaches Walgreens or CVS, or how sterile oncology vials like bortezomib reach US hospitals via GPO contracts. Aurobindo often makes the API in Telangana first. It then formulates the tablet at Unit VII (Jadcherla) or the vial at Eugia. Finally, it clears stock through its New Jersey and Dayton hubs to wholesalers McKesson, Cencora, or Cardinal Health [5][12][22].

2. Europe Formulations (₹10,315 Cr | 30.7% of FY26 sales): Built on the 2014 Actavis deal, Europe is Aurobindo's fastest-growing major region. Sales jumped 23.4% YoY in FY26 to cross €1 billion, then rose another 27% YoY in Q2 FY27 to ₹3,161 crore (€288 million) [2][3][15]. Unlike the US wholesaler model, Aurobindo sells directly to retail pharmacies, hospital tenders, and regional distributors across seven core European markets [13]. Concrete Example: Local brands like Arrow Génériques in France and Puren Pharma in Germany sell Indian-made cardiovascular and antibiotic generics (such as atorvastatin) to community pharmacies. In March 2026, Aurobindo also partnered with STADA Arzneimittel AG to sell CuraTeQ's EMA-approved biosimilars—Dazublys (trastuzumab) and Zefylti (filgrastim)—in Germany and France [11][15].

3. Growth Markets (₹3,499 Cr | 10.4% of FY26 sales): This segment spans Canada, Brazil, Mexico, South Africa, and emerging Asian markets. Revenue grew 10.0% YoY in FY26 ($397 million) and reached ₹980 crore in Q4 FY26 [6]. Concrete Example: In Brazil and Canada, Aurobindo supplies hospital tenders and pharmacy chains with oral-solid cardiovascular and CNS drugs. In January 2026, CuraTeQ won Health Canada's Notice of Compliance (NOC) for biosimilar Dyrupeg (pegfilgrastim) [11]. It followed with Brazil ANVISA GMP approval in July 2026 to access regulated emerging-market biologics tenders [6][11].

4. ARV Formulations (₹1,384 Cr | 4.1% of FY26 sales): Aurobindo supplies triple-combination HIV drugs (such as TLD) to the Global Fund and PEPFAR across Sub-Saharan Africa [6]. Sales rebounded 31.9% YoY in FY26 ($157 million) on tender wins and price revisions. This high-volume business keeps Indian oral-solid plants well utilized [6].

5. Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients — APIs (₹4,047 Cr | 12.0% of FY26 sales): Split between Beta-lactam and Non-beta-lactam APIs, external sales dipped 6.4% in FY26 on softer pricing [2][6]. Revenue then rebounded 12.9% YoY in Q4 FY26 to ₹1,208 crore [2]. External sales understate this unit's true value because captive API feeds Aurobindo's own finished doses. Concrete Example: At Lyfius Pharma's 15,000 MTPA PLI plant in Kakinada, Aurobindo ferments raw Penicillin-G at 800–900 tonnes per month [4][10]. It converts 20–30% in-house into 6-APA and Amoxicillin for US and EU tablets, and sells the rest to Indian antibiotic makers [4][10][16].

web_blocks.title: Emerging Option Engines: CuraTeQ Biosimilars & TheraNym Biologics CDMO
paragraphs: Two biologics engines are now shifting from capex into commercial revenue. First, CuraTeQ Biologics holds EMA approvals for Dazublys (trastuzumab), Zefylti (filgrastim), and Dyrupeg (pegfilgrastim) [11]. It also posted positive Phase 3 data for denosumab and omalizumab (BP11), scaling 10,000 L bioreactor capacity toward a 15-product pipeline by 2029–2030 [3][11].

Second, TheraNym Biologics opened in Hyderabad in mid-2026 with Merck (MSD) as its anchor CDMO client [17]. Unit 1 (15 kL plus fill-finish) is in qualification, while $175 million is committed for Unit 2 (60 kL) to target $150–200 million in annual revenue by the early 2030s [17].

book_paragraphs: To see how Aurobindo Pharma actually makes money, you and I need to look past the ticker and walk through its five operating engines. In FY26, the company generated ₹33,653 crore in consolidated revenue. Roughly 43% came from US Formulations (₹14,408 crore), 31% from Europe (₹10,315 crore), 12% from external APIs (₹4,047 crore), 10% from Growth Markets like Canada and Brazil (₹3,499 crore), and 4% from global HIV anti-retroviral tenders (₹1,384 crore).

Notice what happened in FY26 when the US patent-settlement windfall from generic Revlimid faded. In a less diversified generic company, losing roughly ₹550 crore of high-margin quarterly Revlimid sales would have triggered a sharp earnings contraction. Instead, Europe surged 23.4% to cross €1 billion in annual sales, ARV tenders jumped nearly 32%, and Growth Markets added 10%—allowing consolidated revenue to grow 6.1% while holding operating margins near 20.4%. Then, in Q2 FY27, the US engine roared back with 25% growth to ₹4,555 crore on the back of complex launches like generic Advair and Aurobindo's first NCE, ADQUEY, lifting total quarterly sales to a record ₹10,263 crore.

Every one of these segments connects back to physical chemistry. When a patient in Paris picks up generic atorvastatin from a neighborhood pharmacy, or a hospital in Texas administers sterile pemetrexed through a GPO contract, or a clinic in Kenya dispenses triple-combination HIV tablets funded by PEPFAR, Aurobindo is often supplying both the bulk chemical molecule and the finished dose. At Kakinada, its Lyfius subsidiary is now fermenting 800 to 900 tonnes of Penicillin-G every month, converting a portion into 6-APA and amoxicillin for its own European and American tablets while selling the rest to Indian peers who previously relied on Chinese imports.

On top of those five established engines sit two long-dated biologics bets that are just beginning to leave the hangar: CuraTeQ Biologics, which has already secured European approvals for trastuzumab, filgrastim, and pegfilgrastim and partnered with STADA for EU distribution; and TheraNym Biologics, a contract manufacturing foundry in Hyderabad that landed Merck as its inaugural anchor customer. The breadth is impressive—the critical test in the next chapter is what this sprawling machine costs to run and fund.

Let's zoom in on the US Formulations engine first, because at ₹14,408 crore in FY26 it still drives nearly 43% of the entire company. Within that US bucket sit two very different businesses: legacy retail oral solids—hundreds of everyday tablets and capsules shipped to Walgreens, CVS, Walmart, and the big three wholesalers—and specialty injectables and complex products housed under Eugia and AuroLife. In FY26, generic Revlimid's patent-settlement windfall began tapering off, slicing roughly ₹550 crore off sequential US revenue in the very first quarter. Yet by Q2 FY27, new complex launches such as generic Advair (a respiratory inhaler) and ADQUEY (Aurobindo's first New Chemical Entity in the US) pushed quarterly US revenue up 25% year-on-year to ₹4,555 crore. Meanwhile, Eugia is tracking above $500 million in annual revenue, though its US growth is capped in single digits while Unit III undergoes FDA remediation.

Europe, by contrast, has quietly become Aurobindo's most reliable structural compounder. Growing 23.4% in FY26 to ₹10,315 crore—crossing the €1 billion threshold—and another 27% in Q2 FY27 to ₹3,161 crore, Europe operates on a completely different commercial model from America. Instead of negotiating with three giant wholesalers who can crush margins overnight, Aurobindo's local subsidiaries like Arrow in France and Puren in Germany sell directly to tens of thousands of community pharmacies and regional hospital tenders. That local commercial trust is now paying a second dividend: in March 2026, European pharma major STADA signed on to distribute CuraTeQ's EMA-approved oncology and supportive-care biosimilars across France and Germany.

Finally, do not overlook the Growth Markets, ARV, and API engines that keep Aurobindo's factories humming. Growth Markets (₹3,499 crore in FY26) give Aurobindo footholds in Canada, Brazil, and Mexico—where Health Canada's approval for pegfilgrastim and Brazil ANVISA's GMP clearance open higher-margin biosimilar tenders. ARV formulations (₹1,384 crore, up 32% in FY26) supply life-saving HIV combinations to Global Fund and PEPFAR tenders, absorbing fixed plant overhead. And while external API sales stood at ₹4,047 crore in FY26, the real prize is captive backward integration: Kakinada's Penicillin-G fermentation feeds 6-APA and amoxicillin directly into Aurobindo's own European and US antibiotic lines.

When you and I dissect a multi-engine pharmaceutical business, the first mistake most analysts make is treating all revenue dollars as equal. They are not. A ₹100 crore revenue stream from commodity US oral solids carries completely different margin durability and working-capital intensity than ₹100 crore from European hospital tenders or captive Penicillin-G fermentation. That is why Aurobindo's record ₹10,263 crore quarter in Q2 FY27—up 23.9% year-on-year—deserves a granular look under the hood rather than a headline cheer. Within that print, US revenue jumped 25% to ₹4,555 crore ($477 million) thanks to ten new launches including gAdvair and ADQUEY, while Europe surged 27% to ₹3,161 crore (€288 million).

Look closely at what happens when one engine coughs while another accelerates. In FY26, as high-margin gRevlimid exclusivity tapered off, Aurobindo's US formulations revenue slipped 2.7% for the full year. Five years earlier, a US dip of that sort would have dragged the entire company into an earnings slump. Instead, Europe crossed the €1 billion threshold, Growth Markets expanded to ₹3,499 crore, and consolidated sales still rose 6.1% to ₹33,653 crore with operating margins holding steady near 20.4%. Geographic diversification across 150-plus countries is no longer a slide-deck talking point; it is an active shock absorber.

Even more interesting is how the newer verticals—Pen-G at Kakinada, CuraTeQ's EMA-approved biosimilars, and TheraNym's CDMO—layer onto this base. In FY26, these businesses were still net drags or early-stage contributors. By FY27 and FY28, as Kakinada scales toward 10,000–12,000 metric tonnes and STADA begins commercializing CuraTeQ's oncology and supportive-care biosimilars across France and Germany, Aurobindo's revenue mix should gradually tilt away from pure-play retail oral generics toward higher-barrier fermentation and biologics.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Diversification across US oral solids, European pharmacies, sterile injectables, and bulk fermentation protected Aurobindo from the FY26 gRevlimid cliff. Yet complexity has a price: running 25+ plants across four continents ties up enormous working capital and multiplies the number of regulatory audits that can go wrong.
